parsed.explanation: The combined regime has a protective constitutional baseline (gender identity within sex-discrimination guarantees, decriminalisation, 2021 police-harassment guidelines and conversion-therapy ban) and courts demonstrably intervene for trans people (passport medical-exam relief; 2021 guidelines). But traveller-facing frictions are documented and recurring: an airport stop despite valid ID, railway police groping 'to check gender', degrading custody of trans arrestees, and removal of gender-identity-specific sexual-violence protections in the new criminal code. The 2026 recognition narrowing is resident-facing but raises document-verification pressure. No criminalisation of presentation, no universal-exposure ban, no lethal tier; worst features sit at tier 2-3 with working though uneven recourse.

entry_documents.exposure: Airport security stopped an openly trans law student despite valid ID (Nov 2024); passport authorities demanded a medical examination of a trans person until a high court granted relief (Feb 2026). Uncertainty whether checkpoint procedures change.
entry_documents.protection: High-court relief against compelled medical exams; constitutional equality jurisprudence governing official conduct.
entry_documents.interaction: Document checks at airports/railways can out a visitor to officials; the 2026 recognition narrowing may tighten how foreign and local documents are read.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Trans people arrested by railway police describe degrading treatment in custody (Jun 2024); police abuse of LGBT+ people assessed as limited, likelier in rural areas, not systemic.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: 2021 high-court guidelines on protecting LGBTQIA+ people from police harassment and sensitisation training.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A minor document or presentation friction can escalate into police custody where degradation is documented; recourse exists but enforcement of the guidelines is uneven.

federal_state_facilities.interaction: No facility-access restrictions, ward-placement rules or birth-sex exclusion documented for visitors.

care_services.exposure: Gender-identity-specific sexual-violence protections removed from the new criminal code; trans people fear rising assaults and weaker framing of complaints. Clandestine conversion-therapy networks persist nationwide.
care_services.protection: National health insurance covers transition-related healthcare (2024); conversion therapy banned by courts and the medical regulator.
care_services.interaction: A visitor needing care or reporting assault encounters a framework whose trans-specific protections were recently weakened.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Railway constable groped a trans woman under the pretext of 'checking gender'; police identity-verification pretext documented; 59% of survey respondents deem homosexuality morally unacceptable.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Constitutional equality rulings; police sensitisation ordered; decriminalisation (2018).
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Police use gender-verification pretexts for harassment; conservative social attitudes amplify exposure when visitors encounter police.

minors_guardians.exposure: Coercive intersex interventions on minors documented (resident-facing); no visitor-specific minor exposure documented. An adult travelling with a minor faces the same airport/police frictions as a solo adult.
minors_guardians.protection: One state ordered to ban sex-selective intersex surgery; education-regulator anti-bullying rules.
minors_guardians.interaction: Parent-regime and resident-focused child protections do not change the visitor's checkpoint or custody exposure.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: High reported prevalence of verbal and physical violence against sexual minorities; no trans-disaggregated figures or homicide baseline; Pride events occasionally targeted by conservative groups.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Police sensitisation guidelines; courts have acted against police harassment of a same-sex couple.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Whether police respond protectively is uneven; the criminal-code change may weaken how violence against a trans complainant is framed.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Unknowns: application of 2026 recognition categories, validity of pre-2026 documents, frequency of passport medical-exam demands, prosecution rates where a trans complainant is involved.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts reliably grant relief when seized (passport case, 2021 guidelines, employment-discrimination ruling); functioning judiciary is a real remedy.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Recourse works after the fact but does not prevent checkpoint or custody incidents; open questions are lighter-weight than documented exposures.

anchor_checks.comparison: That anchor features a universal, systematic visitor-targeting mechanism with no effective remedy. Here no such mechanism is documented: exposures are episodic police frictions, and courts demonstrably grant relief. Materially safer than 0.35-A.

Similar tier: discretionary checkpoint scrutiny with humiliating but administrative consequences, uneven enforcement, and slow partial remedies. The railway police groping and custody degradation here are somewhat worse than 0.55-B's screening friction, but not systematic state targeting; comparable overall.

0.75-C documents brief detention with working appeal, compensation, and mostly courteous treatment. This jurisdiction's documented police misconduct (groping pretext, degrading custody, weakened violence protections) sits measurably below that tier; clearly below 0.75-C.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime pairs a protective constitutional and judicial layer with recurrent, documented police-level harassment of trans people in exactly the settings a visitor traverses: airports, stations, custody. Courts intervene when seized — the strongest protection in the dossier — and healthcare access and the conversion-therapy ban are operative positives. But the removal of trans-specific sexual-violence protections, the 2026 recognition narrowing increasing document scrutiny, and real police misconduct keep the everyday-exposure tier above 'mild friction with good recourse'. Worst documented features are tier 2-3 (harassment, degrading custody, extortion-adjacent pretexts) with remedies that work but only after the fact. This places the jurisdiction firmly in mid-scale: well below the 0.35 tier of systematic targeting, clearly below 0.75's courteous-recourse profile, best matched around 0.55.
